summary: SCIM provisioning spike from third-party connector creating privileged invites
description: Issue summary: At ~2026-03-10T08:22Z monitoring alerted on a 15-minute spike in SCIM provisioning events originating from a third-party HR onboarding connector (vendor-hrflow). The majority of created accounts were standard employee accounts, but ~22 accounts were created with a non-default role label that maps to the 'developer-repo-admin' IAM binding. Impact: Potential unauthorized creation of privileged collaborator invites across multiple orgs; risk of lateral privilege escalation if accounts are active. Environment: Production tenant, us-east region. Observed behaviour: Sudden jump from ~2 SCIM events/min to ~240 events/min; provisioning API tokens used exclusively by the vendor connector. Sample events indicate use of a custom 'role' attribute in the SCIM payload that the provisioner incorrectly accepted and mapped to an internal role. Steps to reproduce (investigation steps): 1) Query SCIM audit events in /api/v1/scim/events from 2026-03-10T08:00Z to 2026-03-10T08:40Z. 2) Inspect provisioning token owner: vendor-hrflow@partners.redwood. 3) Replay a sanitized SCIM payload in staging to verify role mapping behavior. 4) Check recent changes to scim-provisioner mapping rules and vendor-facing docs. Logs: See attached audit snippets (log ids scim-20260310-0823-a .. scim-20260310-0835-c) for examples of the rogue role attribute. Initial mitigation performed: Disabled vendor-hrflow SCIM connector token at 2026-03-10T08:28Z; placed an emergency validation rule to reject non-whitelisted role attributes at 2026-03-10T08:35Z.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 08:22Z alert triggered by infra-alerts on provisioning rate. 08:25Z triage by on-call SRE (Arya Patel). 08:28Z token disabled. 08:35Z emergency validation pushed. Findings: - The vendor recently rolled out a 'role' extension to their SCIM payload to request initial repo access. Our mapping table in scim-provisioner treats unknown role strings as 'closest match' using a fuzzy map and a fallback heuristic that in this case selected 'developer-repo-admin'. - The vendor connector made ~4,100 API calls during the 30-minute window; 22 resulted in privileged-role assignments. - No sign of direct credential compromise of the vendor account; vendor support logged a misconfiguration on their side that sent extended attributes in bulk after a CSV import. - Audit trail indicates no privileged actions executed by the newly created accounts (no pushes, no IAM changes) as of investigation time. Hypotheses: (a) Vendor misconfiguration unintentionally forwarded role attribute; (b) A malicious CSV uploaded to vendor portal caused attribute injection; (c) Attack chain via vendor admin account compromise is possible but low confidence. Data collected: SCIM payload samples, token metadata, IP addresses for vendor flows (range 18.197.0.0/16), temporally matched auth logs, and recent deploys affecting scim-provisioner mapping code (deploy ef12ab3). Next steps: 1) Validate whether any invited accounts accepted invites and completed SSO; 2) Force expiry of affected invites and require re-provisioning via manual SR; 3) Run a privileged activity scan for the affected accounts (pushes, permission changes); 4) Engage vendor security (ticket #VND-1924) for root cause and audit; 5) Prepare post-mortem if evidence of compromise found.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:27 - Arya Patel (SRE): Alert looks like a burst from vendor-hrflow token. I'm pausing provisioning rate for that token now.
2026-03-10 08:29 - Maya Chen (Security): Disabled token and added emergency validation rule to scim-provisioner. Noted 22 privileged-role creates. Adding Liam to lead investigation.

2026-03-10 09:10 - Liam O'Connor (IAM): Confirmed mapping heuristic is the root cause. There was a recent fuzzy-role commit (ef12ab3) to reduce mapping errors — it lowered rejections but allowed unknown roles to map to broad admin-like roles. Rolling back that heuristic.

2026-03-10 10:03 - Vendor Security (vendor-hrflow): We reproduced a CSV import bug that augmented an optional role field. We have halted exports and are rotating our connectors. See vendor ticket VND-1924.
2026-03-11 14:22 - Customer Success (Ibrahim Reyes): Reached out to a small set of affected internal teams to verify no suspicious activity. All confirm no account acceptance or push events.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Maya Chen (Security): Recommend a conservative policy: explicit role whitelist for SCIM, deny-by-default for unknown attributes, and 24h manual review for role-granting events from external connectors. Added to follow-up backlog.
resolution: Mitigation steps applied: - Revoked vendor-hrflow SCIM provisioning token and blocked their IP range temporarily. - Rolled back fuzzy-role mapping commit (ef12ab3) and deployed explicit role whitelist in scim-provisioner. - Expired all pending invites associated with the 22 affected provisioning events and required manual re-issue. - Requested vendor rotate their integration credentials and provided remediation guidance. - Performed a privileged-activity scan (no suspicious actions found). Follow-up actions: - Security and IAM to implement permanent deny-by-default mapping and new unit tests for scim attribute handling (owner: Liam O'Connor). - Schedule joint post-incident review with vendor (owner: Maya Chen). Incident remains open pending vendor RCA and completion of follow-up items.
follow_up_items: Implement deny-by-default role mapping in scim-provisioner (owner: Liam O'Connor)
Add unit and integration tests for unknown SCIM attributes (owner: Platform QA)
Vendor RCA and credential rotation confirmation (owner: Vendor Security)
Confluence post-incident writeup and customer notification draft (owner: Security Communications)
